content:
ellie: FYI a dev ran into two linked problems: SDK types are awkward after upgrading to v2 and their Vercel Edge deploy fails with `require is not defined`. They have mixed imports in examples which might be confusing new users.
marco: Do we have a canonical example for ESM + Edge? I think our README has CJS samples still in a few places.
handa: We do, but it's buried. Also our exported types force `ResponsePayload<unknown>` in a lot of helpers, which makes consumer code verbose. Many people prefer `any` as the ergonomic default.
ellie: Error they pasted: `TS2769: No overload matches this call. Overload 1 expects 1 argument, but got 0.` when calling `createClient()` with no args.
marco: Hmm that implies we removed the no-arg overload. We should add `createClient(): Client` and `createClient(opts: ClientOptions): Client` or the generic variants. Keep overloads simple for inference.
handa: Suggestion: export a default-friendly signature `createClient<T = any>(opts?: ClientOptions & { model?: T }): Client<T>` so callers who omit model still get a typed client.
ellie: We need to be careful with `any` vs `unknown` tradeoff. Internal code can use `unknown` but public APIs might default to `any` for ergonomics and provide a strict `createStrictClient` if folks want to opt into stricter generics.
marco: On runtime: Vercel Edge uses esbuild/bundler that prefers ESM. If our package.json still advertises only CJS, their deployed worker will break. We should ensure `exports` has `import` and `require` fields and that dist includes an `esm` build. Example: "exports": {"import":"./dist/esm/index.js","require":"./dist/cjs/index.js"}.
handa: Also add a note to avoid top-level `process.env` reads; use lazy/env getters: `const API_KEY = typeof process !== 'undefined' ? process.env.API_KEY : globalThis.__REDWOOD_API_KEY` so edge friendly.
ellie: Good point. They also hit `Buffer is not defined` in the Edge environment when our polyfill step was skipped by some bundlers. Add doc on polyfills (or avoid Buffer usage).
marco: For TS config, recommend `module: ESNext`, `moduleResolution: bundler`, and `target: ES2020` in examples. Add a snippet to the migration guide.
handa: Also add a tiny Vercel Edge sample repo under examples/edge-minimal that uses `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference/esm'` and a minimal `package.json` with `type: module`. That will reduce onboarding friction.
ellie: Good. On the typing change, create a types PR that: 1) adds a permissive no-arg overload, 2) provides `Client<T = any>` default, 3) exposes `SDKResponse<T = any>` alias, and 4) documents `unknown` vs `any` guidance in migration notes.
marco: Can we also run a quick tsserver test across typical tsconfigs to catch breakages? I'll add a CI job that installs a matrix of TS versions and common tsconfigs.
handa: And a lint rule for examples: no `require(` calls in `examples/edge-*`. Fail CI if CJS patterns are present.
ellie: Perfect. I'll open an issue to track: "dx: types + edge ESM/CJS parity + examples" and link this thread. @devex-bot please create it.
devex-bot: Created issue #3320: "dx: types + edge ESM/CJS parity + examples" and linked this thread.
marco: Thanks. Once the PR is up we should notify the SDK migration doc owners to update snippets.
ellie: Will draft PR tonight and include the minimal edge sample and tsconfig snippet.
handa: Thanks team. If anyone has prior minimized repros, paste them here so we can include.
ellie: I'll attach a tiny repro in the GH issue.
marco: Nice work.
